newsitem.title: USA: Chubb Q2 net premiums up 8.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Chubb Q2 net premiums up 8.8 pct.

text.p: Chubb Corp said on Tuesday net property-casualty premiums written rose 8.8 percent in the second quarter to $1.4 billion.
A portion of this growth is related to the previously announced termination of the quote share reinsurance agreements between Chubb and Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc.
After adjusting for the effects of these reinsurance agreements, second quarter premium growth was 6.6 percent.
Core domestic premiums, excluding the effects of the reinsurance agreements, grew 5.6 percent in the second quarter.
International premiums rose 11.1 percent in the second quarter, Chubb said.
International growth continues to meet expectations although the reported figures for the second quarter were somewhat depressed by currency translation, Chubb said.
The second quarter combined ratio fell to 95.3 percent from 96.3 percent a year ago, Chubb said.
Chubb said its personal lines business turned in a strong performance with core premium growth of 9.3 percent and a combined ratio of 84.4 percent.
In commercial lines, core premium growth was 6.1 percent and the combined ratio was 98.7 percent.

"Results for our executive protection and financial institutions businesses remain particularly strong, despite tough competition in these areas, as in all others," Chubb chief executive Dean O'Hare said.
"New products and product extensions, among them employment practices liability and liability coverages for privately held companies, are being enthusiastically received in the marketplace," he said.

Chubb said its real estate business recorded losses after taxes of $6.4 million for the quarter and $5.2 million for the six months as a result of an adjustment to the carrying value of certain assets.

This reflects the terms of the agreement reached in June to sell a substantial portion of Chubb's commercial real estate properties to a joint venture company formed by PaineWebber Real Estate Securities Inc and Morgan Stanley Real Estate Fund II L.P
In 1996, real estate income was $3.0 million for the quarter and $7.0 million for the six months.
Chubb repurchased 2.2 million shares of common stock in the second quarter bringing the total purchases in 1997 to nearly 8.0 million.

In the second quarter, Chubb Capital Corp called for redemption of the remaining outstanding exchangeable subordinated notes. Prior to the redemption date, the holders of the notes elected to convert the notes into shares of common stock, resulting in the issuance of nearly 5.0 million shares.
